note: The paper quotes a 33-repository corpus. This directory holds 30 run.json payloads.
The difference is not a discrepancy: 35 repositories were mined, 5 came back
backfill_capped, psycopg is dropped as a documented incomplete mine (~16h to genesis),
and Complex-YOLOv3 is void (perfect 1.00 against a mismatched tree). So the 33 = the 30
here, minus Complex-YOLOv3, plus the 4 capped repositories driven to completion.
Those 4 have no run.json here because their clones did not survive; their settled values
are recorded below with the ledger line that reports each one.
Two payloads here also predate the F72 fix to sgt's tracked-path lister (git ls-files
C-quotes non-ASCII names, the pre-fix lister mis-parsed them and is_file() swallowed the
result), so their fsck_tree lists omit files sgt cannot reproduce and their rates are
~10 points too high. The corrected values are recorded below. Regenerating them from the
payloads would need fsck --tree re-run under the current lens, which mines on contact.
verify.py reproduces every published corpus figure from this file plus the payloads.

how_to_remeasure: Both values are re-measured, not only quoted. fsck_tree mines on contact, so copy the
clone first and never run this against /tmp/v3 itself:
scope  = {p for p in tracked_paths if not through_symlink(p)
Both come back to four decimals. The stored payloads differ from fresh only in
backstop_kept, by exactly the files F72's path-lister fix stopped swallowing.

why: retention.py recomputes grounded/store from the archived stores and gives
rho = +0.544 and median 0.788, not the published +0.549 and 0.79. Two known reasons,
neither resolvable from committed material: the four settled rows survive in the ledger
at two decimals only, and the original script's 'grounded' differs slightly from
order._grounded over the whole store -- bleak comes back 1697 grounded of an identical
4901-op store where the ledger recorded 1693. The _grounded rewrite predates the
measurement (2026-07-18), so the algorithm is not the difference; the candidate set is,
and the script that chose it lived in /tmp. Checked with a tolerance for that reason.

open: Resolved: the ledger's two MiroFish rates were two different corrections to the same
published 0.8866, never composed -- 0.7835 is the F65 scope pass (21 failures of 97) and
0.7938 the F72 lister rescore (20 of 97). Re-measuring on a copy under the current product
gives 0.7938 exactly, so that is the settled value; the one-file gap is a classification
difference under the pre-F72 lister and does not move any rank statistic.
run.json records the store size (fsck.checked) but no grounded count, so retention had no
committed inputs at all. retention.py now recomputes it from the archived stores, which
closes the gap to a tolerance rather than to an exact match; see
published_within_tolerance above. Reconciling the last ~0.005 needs the definition of
'grounded' used by the original script, which did not survive /tmp.
